subject: Post-demo: private gateway & egress budget qualification

Subject: Post-demo: private gateway & egress budget qualification

Hi Samir / QuantWare ops team —

Thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the performance SLOs and the network items we need to validate for your private/VPC deployment so we can lock down the acceptance criteria for the POC. Below is a concise recap + action items.

Quick recap of customer goals (as I understood them):
- Live streaming inference for market data enrichment at 20 concurrent streams (each ~60 tokens/sec peak)
- P95 generation latency target: <= 120ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput targeting 150K tokens/minute during peak windows (burst to 300K)
- Egress constraint: outbound traffic must flow through QuantWare VPN gateway to their firewall (no public egress from hosts)

Network / performance questions we need to confirm:
1) VPN / Peering throughput: what sustained TCP bandwidth can your gateway support for a single peered tunnel? We are seeing ~1.2–1.8 Gbps required for a 150K tokens/minute target with batching + streaming.
2) Latency budget inside VPC: please confirm additional hop budget from peering to your application cluster (typical target is <= 15ms one-way internal).
3) MTU and fragmentation: any restrictions on jumbo frames? Our streaming paths benefit from MTU >= 9000 in some setups.
4) Keepalives & TCP idle timeouts: streaming clients hold long-lived connections — any aggressive NAT timeouts?
5) Egress inspection / proxy: will TLS interception or an outbound proxy be in path (this can add 40–120ms per request in some deployments).

Requested deliverables (by end of next week if possible):
- Network trace (pcap) of a 5–10 minute live session (sample traces attached)
- Confirmation of sustained tunnel bandwidth (or a runbook for ramp/testing)
- Contact for your infra/ops who can run a perf test with us (we can provide a small load harness)

Next steps I propose:
- Diego + Karthik to run an initial synthetic streaming test on Wednesday 2027-08-25 (requesting QuantWare ops to join or run locally)
- QuantWare to provide a network pcap and gateway config by EOW 2027-08-27
- After traces, Marissa will propose the POC acceptance checklist and SLA gating items

Attachments: [Attachment: network-trace-20270821.pcap (pcap) - 3.8MB], [Attachment: quantware-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (xlsx) - 120KB]

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on another 30-min follow-up if you want to go line-by-line.

Best,

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below, and we'll attach the pcap from our side shortly.

Answers:
- Gateway throughput: the appliance is an HA pair, each supporting up to 2.5 Gbps sustained per tunnel. We typically cap a single tunnel to 2 Gbps for headroom.
- Internal hop budget: peering -> app cluster is 8–12ms average (we're on same AZ backbone), worst-case 18ms under load.
- MTU: we run standard 1500; jumbo frames are not enabled due to our firewall chain.
- Idle timeouts: 15 minutes before NAT translation cleanup; we can configure TCP keepalives to 60s.
- TLS inspection: outbound TLS interception is enabled for HTTP ports; it does not inspect raw TCP on custom ports.

We will attach: the requested 7-minute pcap (sample of streaming session) and our gateway config extract. Ops team says they can run your harness; Nina from our partner integration team (cc'd) will coordinate test windows.

Two clarifying asks from our side:
1) For the streaming path, can Redwood support a degraded fallback that routes to hosted endpoints if the peered tunnel hits >85% utilization? We'd like graceful degradation thresholds documented.
2) What's the expected token-per-second to bandwidth ratio you used to estimate 1.2–1.8 Gbps? Helps us map our observed telemetry to your sizing.

Thanks — Samir

Samir / Diego — quick engineering notes from my side after reviewing the initial numbers and what we saw in the live demo: 

- Bandwidth math: our conservative estimate assumes ~50 bytes per token on average (including websocket/frame overhead and TLS). For 150K tokens/minute that is ~= 125 KB/s ~ 1.0 Gbps. Burst to 300K pushes to ~2.0 Gbps. These figures depend heavily on batching, per-message framing, and whether responses are deltas (streaming) or full-message chunks.
- Concurrency & sockets: 20 concurrent streams with persistent connections is fine; the main ops risk is SYN/FIN churn if clients reconnect frequently. Set keepalive to 60s and monitor idle counts.
- Latency budget: to meet P95 120ms we need < 20ms p2p inside the peered environment and < 60ms external e2e for end-user client RTTs. If your peering worst-case climbs to 18ms under load we're borderline — will need to tune batching and prefetch windows.
- Fallback: we can implement automatic fallback to a hosted model variant filtered by rules: if tunnel utilization > 80% OR p95 backend latency > 200ms for 1 minute, switch to hosted. There is a short failover window (~2–3s) and a quality delta we should document in the MOP.

Action items for engineering tests:
- QuantWare ops to run our small load harness (we provide container) during a low-impact window. Target: 30 minute ramp, 10 minute sustained at 150K tokens/min.
- QuantWare to share pcap + firewall/gw logs (we need TLS-allowed packet headers to verify RTTs).
- Diego/Marissa to capture runbook steps for fallback and SLA gating.

I'll be available Wednesday for the test.

Thanks,
